info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance — Unit 8: Simulation: line-station turnaround. CEFR B2. Formative quiz split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How much ground time does the team have for the turnaround?

generalfeedback.text: Raivis says: "we only have forty-five minutes of ground time". Ground time is the total time the aircraft is on the ground.

feedback.text: Correct — "forty-five minutes of ground time".
That is the ground time in the later voicemail (Flight 621), not Dialogue 1.
No — the turnaround is described as "extremely tight".
No — that would not be a tight turnaround.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What defect did Anna find on the walkaround?

generalfeedback.text: "On the right engine cowl, one access panel is loose, and two fasteners are missing."

feedback.text: Correct — a loose access panel with two fasteners missing.

answer.text: A cracked windscreen on the flight deck

feedback.text: No — the defect is on the right engine cowl.

answer.text: A flat main-wheel tyre on the parking stand

feedback.text: No — no tyre is mentioned in the handover.

answer.text: An oil leak from the right engine cowling

feedback.text: No — the oil is finished; the open item is the panel.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Anna recorded the defect in the tech log and opened a task card for the panel.

generalfeedback.text: True. "the defect is documented in the tech log, and I opened a task card for the panel."

feedback.text: Correct — both the tech log entry and the task card are done.
Listen again — she confirms both are complete.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many fasteners are missing from the access panel? (Write a number.)

generalfeedback.text: Two fasteners are missing: "two fasteners are missing".

feedback.text: Correct — two fasteners.
Listen again — a specific number is said.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What does the BITE test show?

generalfeedback.text: "The BITE shows an open circuit, so one sensor connector is probably loose."

feedback.text: Correct — an open circuit on the sensor connector.

answer.text: A short circuit to the airframe ground

feedback.text: No — the fault is an open circuit, not a short.
No — the fault is electrical, on the sensor circuit.
No — the readout points to the panel sensor connector.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The missing clip makes this an AOG situation.

generalfeedback.text: False. "Stores holds one clip, therefore it is not an AOG." AOG means a missing part stops the departure.

feedback.text: Correct — stores has the clip, so it is not an AOG.
Listen again — the part is available in stores.

questiontext.text: Listen to the duty voicemail (Dialogue 4) again. How many minutes of ground time does Flight 621 have? (Write a number.)

generalfeedback.text: "the ground time is only thirty-five minutes" — 35 minutes.

feedback.text: Correct — thirty-five minutes.
That is Dialogue 1. The voicemail says thirty-five.

questiontext.text: Listen to the duty voicemail (Dialogue 4) again. At what time does Flight 621 arrive? Write it as four digits (for example 1830).

generalfeedback.text: "Flight six two one arrives at nineteen forty" — 1940 (19:40).

feedback.text: Correct — nineteen forty, 1940.
That is when the slot closes in the dispatch message, not the arrival time.

questiontext.text:
Read the tech log page.

Defect 2: cowl hinge cracked. MEL reference 71-10-01 applies, so the defect may be carried as a deferred defect.

What does the MEL reference allow the team to do?

generalfeedback.text: When the MEL applies, a defect may be carried now and rectified later — a deferred defect.

answer.text: Carry it as a deferred defect

feedback.text: Correct — the MEL permits the defect to be carried.

answer.text: Rectify it fully before the aircraft flies again

feedback.text: No — the MEL allows a deferral; full rectification is later.

answer.text: Ground the aircraft until the next base check

feedback.text: No — the aircraft may dispatch with the deferral in place.

answer.text: Request a new departure slot from the tower

feedback.text: No — the MEL is about airworthiness, not slot timing.

questiontext.text:
Read the dispatch message.

Part: the clip, part number C-4402, is serviceable and is available in stores, so there is no AOG.

The clip has to be flown in from another station.

generalfeedback.text: False. The clip is in stores and serviceable, so there is no AOG and nothing needs to be flown in.

feedback.text: Correct — the part is already available in stores.
Re-read — the clip is available in stores.

questiontext.text:
Read the dispatch message.

Warning: the cowl hinge is not a no-go item, but the panel sensor must be serviceable before dispatch.

What must be serviceable before the aircraft can dispatch?

generalfeedback.text: The panel sensor must be serviceable — that is why the team runs a BITE test and clears the warning.

feedback.text: Correct — the panel sensor must be serviceable before dispatch.
No — the message names the panel sensor.
No — that is not mentioned in the message.
No — the serviceability item is the panel sensor.

questiontext.text:
Read the dispatch message.

Timing: sign the release to service before pushback. We cannot accept a delay, because the slot closes at twenty ten.

At what time does the slot close? Write it as four digits (for example 1830).

generalfeedback.text: "the slot closes at twenty ten" — 2010 (20:10).

feedback.text: Correct — twenty ten, 2010.
That is the arrival time in the voicemail, not the slot-close time here.

name.text: R5 · Task card · order of actions

questiontext.text:
Read the task-card note.

Documentation: record every action in the tech log, and close each task card before you sign the release.

You should sign the release to service first, and then close the task card.

generalfeedback.text: False. The card is closed before the release is signed: "close each task card before you sign the release".

feedback.text: Correct — close the card first, then sign the release.
Re-read the order: close the card before you sign.

questiontext.text:
Use the correct form of the verb. Write one word in the gap.

Secure the panel before the aircraft ______ (depart) for pushback.

generalfeedback.text: After before, use the present tense: departs, not "will depart".

feedback.text: Correct — present tense after before.
No — do not use will in a time clause. Use "departs".
The verb is "departs" — present tense after before.

name.text: U2 · time clause · as soon as

questiontext.text:
Use the correct form of the verb. Write one word in the gap.

As soon as the clip ______ (arrive), we will fit it.

generalfeedback.text: After as soon as, use the present tense: arrives. The main clause keeps will.

feedback.text: Correct — present tense after as soon as.
No — the time clause takes the present: "arrives".
The verb is "arrives" — present tense after as soon as.

questiontext.text:
Use the correct form of the verb. Write one word in the gap.

After I ______ (finish) the walkaround, I will call you.

generalfeedback.text: After after, use the present tense: finish. Only the main clause has will.

feedback.text: Correct — present tense after after.
No — will belongs only in the main clause. Use "finish".
The verb is "finish" — present tense after after.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the underlined part correctly. Write two words.

Check the MEL before to defer the defect.

generalfeedback.text: No infinitive after before. Use a clause — you defer — or the -ing form "deferring".

feedback.text: Correct — a clause after before.
Also correct — the -ing form works after before.
No — do not use the infinitive after before.
Use "you defer" or "deferring" after before.

questiontext.text:
Use the correct form of the verb. Write one word in the gap.

We cannot dispatch until the warning ______ (clear).

generalfeedback.text: After until, use the present tense: clears, not "will clear".

feedback.text: Correct — present tense after until.
No — use the present: "clears".
The verb is "clears" — present tense after until.

questiontext.text:
Write the one term that fits.

To release and send the aircraft out for its next flight is to ______ it.

generalfeedback.text: dispatch — to release and send the aircraft onward.

feedback.text: Correct — dispatch the aircraft.
No — rectify means to fix a defect fully.
The term is "dispatch".

questiontext.text:
Write the one term that fits.

To repair a defect completely, so it is no longer a fault, is to ______ it.

generalfeedback.text: rectify — to fix a defect fully. Compare with "defer", which means fix it later.

feedback.text: Correct — rectify a defect.
No — defer means carry it now and fix it later.
The term is "rectify".

name.text: V1 · terms and meanings · set A

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: MEL = the list of what may be inoperative for dispatch; tech log = the aircraft logbook for defects and actions; AOG = a missing part that stops departure; BITE = the built-in self-test that shows fault codes; serviceable = fit to use and legal to fit or fly.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some matches are correct — check the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: the list of what may be inoperative for dispatch
the aircraft logbook for defects and actions
a missing part that stops the departure
the built-in self-test that shows fault codes
fit to use and legal to fit or to fly

name.text: V2 · terms and meanings · set B

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: handover = passing the job to the next technician; walkaround = the visual check around the aircraft; slot = the fixed time window to depart; task card = the job document with the steps.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some matches are correct — check the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: passing the job to the next technician
the visual check around the aircraft
the fixed time window to depart
the job document with the steps

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which verb goes with "the release to service"?

generalfeedback.text: You sign the release to service — the certifying signature that the aircraft is fit to fly.

feedback.text: Correct — you sign the release to service.
No — "make" does not collocate here. Use "sign".
No — you open a task card, but you sign a release.
No — the natural verb is "sign".

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which phrase means to keep the departure window you already have?

generalfeedback.text: You hold the slot — keep the fixed departure window by avoiding a delay.

feedback.text: Correct — hold the slot.
No — the fixed collocation is "hold the slot".
No — "save" does not collocate here. Use "hold".
No — you already have the slot; you "hold" it.
